newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.
newsitem.headline: CWB details Prairie elevator space, railcar unload.

text.p: Vacant primary elevator space continued to tighten in the past week across Canada's Prairies while railcar unloads at Pacific ports reached near their target levels, Canadian Wheat Board said.
Average vacancy in Prairie elevators was 17 percent in the week ended February 23, compared to 18 percent the week before and 21 percent the week before that.

Weather and equipment-related difficulties in shipping grains and oilseeds to Pacific ports from the Prairies since early January caused vessel backlogs on the coast and lead to tightening primary elevator space.
Forty eight ships waited to load on Canada's Pacific coast on Friday. One ship was berthed for 50 days.
Manitoba elevators had the least space available with 15 percent vacant, followed by Alberta at 17 percent and Saskatchewan at 18 percent.
Vancouver saw 2,972 railcar unloaded in the past week, compared to the target of 3,000 hopper cars.
Prince Rupert unloads reached 1,105 hopper cars compared to the target of 1,300.
Thunder Bay unloads totalled 499 hopper cars, above the 490 target.
